lyrics:
[Intro: whistled melody over clean electric guitar]

[Verse 1: high clear male tenor, gentle]
I take her by the hand along the river
There's a line of stones set in the ground
She hops across it on her scooter
Never looks down, never slows down

[Verse 2: bass and soft drums enter]
I was twenty when I stood here
With a hammer and a stranger's wine
We sang until our voices went
I kept a piece. It's on a shelf of mine.

[Chorus: full band, soaring, whistle answering]
Where the wall was
There are bicycles and trees
Where the wall was
There's a kid who can't believe
That anybody ever stopped a street
She asked me what a border is
Where the wall was

[Verse 3: voice warmer, guitars chiming]
I tell her there were soldiers
I tell her there were lights
She says, "But why?" and I've got nothing
She says, "That's silly." She is right.

[Chorus: full band, soaring, whistle answering]
Where the wall was
There are bicycles and trees
Where the wall was
There's a kid who can't believe
That anybody ever stopped a street
She asked me what a border is
Where the wall was

[Guitar Solo: lyrical, over the chorus chords]

[Bridge: half-time, voice and acoustic guitar]
They told us it would stand a hundred years
They told us nothing ever moves
Remember that, the next time

[Final Chorus: biggest, crowd singing, whistle on top]
Where the wall was
There are bicycles and trees
Where the wall was
There's a kid who can't believe
That anybody ever stopped a street
She asked me what a border is
Where the wall was

[Outro: whistled melody alone, a scooter rolling away]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 76 BPM, 4/4, C major. A slow, hopeful rock ballad with a march in its step.

VOICE: Male tenor, high, clear and slightly accented, gentle in the verses and ringing in the choruses. He whistles the main tune at the start and end, and a crowd joins the final chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: A whistled melody, a clean electric guitar arpeggio, acoustic guitar, bass, a drum kit with a steady, stately beat, a second electric guitar with a singing lead tone, a string pad, crowd voices.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, whistle. 0:22 Verse 1. 0:52 Verse 2. 1:22 Chorus 1. 1:56 Verse 3. 2:26 Chorus 2. 3:00 Guitar solo. 3:22 Bridge. 3:40 Final chorus. 4:12 Outro, whistle and a scooter, ends 4:28.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 1990 European rock ballad: clean, wide and anthemic, guitars bright, whistle dry and close.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'She asked me what a border is' at 1:46.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original stands in the moment of change, hoping. This stands thirty-five years later on the same ground with a child for whom the change is so complete that it has to be explained.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Remembering, amazed, humbled, hopeful.
